You are a code worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit, push or touch .git. Do NOT run a formatter on YAML or markdown (run `uv run ruff format` on the Python files you change). You own only: data/stories/continuity-initiative/knowledge.yaml, storygame/story_package/models.py, storygame/story_package/loader.py, storygame/runtime/narration_safety.py, docs/markdown-story-authoring.md, docs/world-model-grounding.md, tests/test_leak_terms.py (new), tests/test_knowledge_projection.py, tests/test_narration_safety.py. Edit nothing else. The engine must stay story-neutral: no story nouns in code.

Goal: separate the narration LEAK vocabulary of a knowledge item from its RECALL aliases and its DELIVERY (must_convey) synonyms. Today every item alias and every multi-word must_convey phrase becomes a leak term in KnowledgeIndexes.term_to_knowledge (loader.py ~line 331-350), so adding a useful alias or a delivery synonym silently adds a guard, and generic phrases the narrator uses naturally ('coded message', 'archive crisis', 'escape route') get the narration rejected.

Design (follow exactly):
1. models.py: add to the knowledge item model an optional field `leak_terms: tuple[str, ...] | None = None`. None means 'not reviewed': keep today's behaviour. A list (even empty) means 'reviewed': it is the item's complete knowledge leak vocabulary.
2. models.py KnowledgeIndexes: add `leak_term_to_knowledge: Mapping[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}`. KEEP `term_to_knowledge` exactly as it is today (aliases + multi-word must_convey). It has a third reader, `_auto_attribute_committed_knowledge` in storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py, that uses it to attach grounding to already-earned items; that must not change, so do not edit cloudflare.py.
3. loader.py: build `leak_term_to_knowledge` with the same term_lookup_forms normalisation. For an item whose leak_terms is None, add its alias forms and multi-word must_convey forms (exactly today's set). For an item whose leak_terms is a list, add only the forms of the listed phrases (an empty list adds nothing). Shared terms keep every owner: one item's list never removes another item's ownership. Validate in the loader that every listed leak term, once normalised, also appears in that item's alias forms or its multi-word must_convey forms or statement? NO: do not add such a constraint; a leak term may be any phrase. Single-word phrases are allowed in the field but the scan only guards multi-word ones, as today.
4. loader.py ~line 600-640 (the check that scene prose does not contain an unavailable knowledge term): use leak_term_to_knowledge instead of term_to_knowledge for `guarded_terms` and `owners`, so the loader and the runtime scan agree on the effective guarded vocabulary. audience_to_known_terms stays as is (it is only a candidate list; filter it through leak_term_to_knowledge).
5. narration_safety.py `_validate_segments`: in the `known_terms` set and the `for form in known_terms` loop use leak_term_to_knowledge (both the membership filter and the `knowledge_ids = set(...get(form, ()))` lookup, and the entity_alias lookups stay as they are). Do NOT change the protected_terms loop, the entity-alias loop, the world protected-knowledge handling or any exemption. Entity alias checks and world.protected_knowledge are independent of leak_terms.
6. Explicit empty leak_terms does not make an item earned and does not bypass the protected-term or unavailable-entity checks.

Story migration in knowledge.yaml (data only; do not touch statement, delivery_text, cue_text, action_evidence, earn_when, requires, establishes, source):
 a. k_sl_2c_d_r1: restore the first must_convey group to `[Michelle's encrypted message, coded message, message, Michelle's coded note, encrypted message from Michelle]`. Add `leak_terms:` listing exactly today's effective multi-word guard vocabulary of this item WITHOUT 'coded message', "Michelle's encrypted message" and 'encrypted message from Michelle'. Compute it with a script from the current file (aliases plus multi-word must_convey phrases from the current groups, minus those three; keep "Michelle's coded note", 'maintenance access route', 'maintenance path', 'local access route', 'route to Michelle', "Rebecca's secured office", "Rebecca's office", 'secured office', "Rebecca's locked office", 'open the detention cells', 'open the cells', 'rescue the prisoners', 'release the prisoners', 'broadcast the evidence', 'transmit the evidence', 'broadcast proof', 'send the evidence', and the alias 'combined broadcast rescue plan known'). Write it in the file's existing flow style.
 b. k_sl_2c_d_r2: restore 'coded message' in the first must_convey group (`[Michelle's maintenance code, maintenance code, coded message, Michelle's code]`) and add `leak_terms:` with today's effective multi-word set of this item minus 'coded message'. Compute it the same way.
 c. k_bridge_2b_archive_crisis: restore the alias so aliases are `[archive crisis, Michelle's resistance]` and add `leak_terms: [Michelle's resistance]`.
 d. k_scene_3c_entry: restore aliases `[escape route, exposure]` and add `leak_terms: []`.
 Do not add leak_terms to any other item.

Tests (hermetic, no network):
 - tests/test_leak_terms.py (new) with a SYNTHETIC package built the way an existing test builds a second package (see tests/test_world_second_package.py and tests/_legacy_package.py for helpers); use unrelated nouns (for example a recall alias 'sealed letter' and a leak term 'silver tunnel password'). Cases: field absent leaves behaviour unchanged (leak index equals term_to_knowledge); a recall-only alias still retrieves its item via alias_to_knowledge and harmless narration using it passes the scan; an explicit leak term rejects before the item is earned with code narration_known_term_leak; adding a must_convey synonym to an item with explicit leak_terms does not add a guard; shared-term ownership survives another item's explicit empty list; an explicit empty list does not bypass world protected terms or the unavailable-entity check; a rejected turn leaves the runtime snapshot unchanged; the loader trap check and the runtime agree.
 - In tests/test_narration_safety.py add, using the same state-building style as the existing test_scene_2c_accepts_encrypted_message_wording_before_reveal, cases on the real package: 'Kristin opens the coded message from Michelle.' accepted in scene 2C before the reveal; and the maintenance-route sentence 'Kristin follows the maintenance access route into the holding block.' still rejected, in the same state, plus 'Kristin sees that Rebecca's secured office can broadcast the evidence.' still rejected, plus 'Kristin hears the cells can be opened. Open the detention cells.' ... if that last wording is accepted, drop it and note which wording you used. Keep the existing tests passing; update test_knowledge_projection.py only where it pinned term_to_knowledge for the restored phrases (those restored terms are in term_to_knowledge again; add assertions on leak_term_to_knowledge for the same phrases expecting set()).
 - Document the new optional field in one short paragraph in docs/markdown-story-authoring.md (what it is, that absent means unreviewed, empty list means no guarded vocabulary) and one bullet under 'Names' in docs/world-model-grounding.md. Plain words. Do not add dated results.

Write ./notes.md listing files changed, the exact leak_terms lists you computed, any wording you substituted, and test results.
